title: The non-inflammatory effect of neuronal NLRP3 on spatial memory after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome has emerged as a critical regulator in neuroinflammatory responses to various brain insults from traumatic, ischemic and neurodegenerative conditions, an effect almost exclusively attributed to microglial NLRP3. Here, we demonstrated that in the absence of changes in inflammatory factors IL-18, IL-1β and TNF-α, neuronal Nlrp3 knockout in hippocampus (nNlrp3-/-) improved long-term spatial memory performance, with increased synaptic proteins levels and enhanced amplitude of long-term potentiation at 4 weeks after traumatic brain injury (TBI), compared to wildtype littermates. Notably, the nNlrp3-/- mice out-performed microglia-specific knockout and global Nlrp3 knockout mice in cognition and synaptic function. We further identified that NLRP3 structurally and functionally directly interacted with the R1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NR1) in hippocampus after TBI. Accordingly, pharmacological inhibition of NLRP3 by MCC950 rescued the decrease in the NMDAR-gated calcium influx by LPS-stimulated hippocampal neurons while selective Nlrp3 knockout in hippocampal neurons partially reversed the decreased phosphorylation level of NR1 after TBI. Collectively, this study provides the first evidence that neuronal NLRP3 constitutes a non-inflammatory response to control synaptic plasticity and cognitive function via NR1-dependent non-inflammatory mechanism in TBI and thus broadens the central role of NLRP3 in neuronal adaptive mechanisms to include both microglial NLRP3-inflammation arm and the neuronal NLRP3-synaptic plasticity arm.

title: Nonpharmacological Interventions in Degenerative Cerebellar Ataxia: A Systematic Review.
abstract: A comprehensive synthesis of nonpharmacological interventions (NPI) in degenerative cerebellar ataxia will clarify their efficacy and inform clinical practice and trial design in a field with limited therapeutic options. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review was conducted (PROSPERO CRD42025649802). PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to April 16, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized interventional studies evaluating rehabilitation, speech therapy, noninvasive neuromodulation (repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial direct current stimulation [tDCS]), virtual reality, vibration therapy, biofeedback-based, assistive devices, and complementary approaches were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklists. Given substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were consolidated narratively. A total of 100 studies met inclusion criteria. Structured physical therapy, rTMS, and tDCS demonstrated statistically significant short-term reductions in ataxia severity (measured using Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia [SARA] or International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale [ICARS]). Improvements were most consistent in axial domains, including gait and postural control. Limited mechanistic studies reported restoration of cerebellar inhibitory modulation, increased cerebellar-frontal connectivity, and enhanced regional perfusion following tDCS. Evidence for speech therapy, virtual reality-based rehabilitation, vibration therapy and complementary approaches was limited. Across all modalities, durability beyond the short-term remained unclear. NPI may confer short-term symptomatic and functional benefits in degenerative cerebellar ataxia, particularly in axial motor domains, supported by the largest evidence for structured rehabilitation followed by neuromodulation, although heterogeneous. Future multicenter, biomarker-informed trials are required to define optimal dosing, durability and stage-specific therapeutic strategies.

title: Psychological and Neurodevelopmental Correlates of Extreme Demand Avoidance in a Clinical Sample, an Exploratory Study.
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Extreme/pathological demand avoidance (EDA) is a behavioral profile characterized by the avoidance of everyday demands, with significant impact on the individuals and those around them. Little is understood regarding the correlates and drivers of EDA; understanding these better may lead to targeted interventions and support strategies. Cross-sectional data from parent-rated measures were analyzed for 63 children referred to a specialist neurodevelopmental clinic in the United Kingdom. The relationship between EDA traits and a number of psychological (intolerance of uncertainty, anxiety, emotional dysregulation [reactivity and dysphoria], cognitive inflexibility, alexithymia [i.e., difficulty identifying emotions]), and neurodevelopmental (autistic and ADHD) traits was tested. No differences in EDA traits were found by diagnostic group (autistic vs. not-autistic) or gender (male and female). Across the whole sample, EDA traits were negatively correlated with age and positively correlated with emotional dysregulation reactivity, ADHD traits, cognitive inflexibility, intolerance of uncertainty and alexithymia. EDA was not associated with autistic traits or anxiety. Path models were used to identify which cognitive and behavioral features predicted EDA scores, once inter-correlations among predictors were controlled for. Only emotional dysregulation, ADHD traits and age predicted EDA-Q scores. Further research is needed to assess how these variables contribute to EDA in larger more diverse samples, capturing potentially unmeasured variables, and exploring possible mediation pathways.

title: Nonlinear absorber device to treat essential tremor: The TREM-AB open-label pilot study.
abstract: Essential tremor (ET) is the most common movement disorder. Medical treatments are not always effective and can have side effects. Surgical interventions are not an option for all patients and can also have debilitating side effects. This project aims to develop a passive nonlinear vibration absorber namely, Nonlinear Energy Sink (NES), to reduce tremors in ET patients. Five ET patients were enrolled. Tremor was assessed clinically using the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) rating scale and electrophysiological recording before and after short-duration device use. The NES bracelet led to a reduction of the FTM score of 32.1% (±19%) while tremor power was reduced by 49.2% (±23.4%) compared to baseline for the arm treated. No side effect was noted. The anti-tremor NES device shows promising results needing to be confirmed in larger controlled studies.

title: Corrigendum to "Glibenclamide treatment improved intraspinal blood volume, tissue sparing, and functional recovery after cervical spinal cord injury in rats" [Brain Res. Bull. 246 (2026) 112162].
Closed-Loop Targeted Memory Reactivation During Sleep Spindles Enhances Motor Memory Consolidation.
abstract: Sleep spindles are thought to facilitate motor memory consolidation by reactivating recently acquired memory traces during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, yet most human evidence is correlational. Using a closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (CL-TMR) protocol, this study tested whether auditory cueing time-locked to spindles enhances the consolidation of a newly acquired motor sequence. Twenty-six young adults practiced two eight-element, explicitly known, sequences of finger movements, each paired with a distinct auditory cue. During subsequent NREM Stage 2 and 3 nighttime sleep, a portable deep-learning-based EEG device (Portiloop) detected spindles online and selectively replayed the cue associated with one sequence (TMR condition), while the other served as a within-subject non-reactivated control (non-TMR) condition. Behavioural performance was assessed before and after sleep. Greater overnight improvements in performance were observed for the reactivated as compared to the non-reactivated condition, hence demonstrating enhanced consolidation following spindle-locked CL-TMR. The magnitude of this TMR benefit was positively correlated with the percentage of stimulations delivered during true spindles. Furthermore, a higher percentage of stimulations occurring during spindle trains (i.e., two or more spindles separated by 6 s apart) was associated with reduced gains. These findings provide further evidence that spindle-timed reactivation supports motor memory consolidation in humans and suggest that spindle trains may represent a favourable physiological window for closed-loop interventions.

Target-site resistance and an altered glyphosate metabolite profile in invasive Cenchrus setaceus populations from southern Spain.
abstract: Cenchrus setaceus is an invasive perennial grass spreading along Mediterranean and southern Atlantic transport corridors in the Iberian Peninsula. Recurrent glyphosate use in roadside vegetation management may impose sustained selection for resistance. We characterized whole-plant glyphosate response and candidate resistance mechanisms in 10 populations collected in southern Spain. Three populations (S, CO3, and SE2) were susceptible, whereas seven populations had GR₅₀ values of 804.0-1108.6 g ae ha-1 and resistance factors of 20.3-28.0. Foliar spray retention and 14C-glyphosate absorption and distribution did not differ among populations at 96 h after treatment. In metabolism studies, the amount of glyphosate at 0 HAT was similar among populations. At 96 HAT, CO1, MA1, MA2, and SE1 contained less glyphosate and more aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA) than the susceptible populations. Analyte identity was confirmed against authentic standards by reversed-polarity capillary electrophoresis. Because only one post-treatment time was evaluated, these data describe an endpoint profile and do not estimate a metabolic rate. CA1, CA2, CO2, and MA1 carried a Pro-106-Ser substitution and showed markedly reduced EPSPS sensitivity. Similar basal EPSPS activity among populations provided no biochemical evidence of constitutive EPSPS overexpression. Overall, resistance-associated traits differed among populations, indicating that no single resistance pattern explains all cases and underscoring the need to diversify roadside management beyond repeated glyphosate use.

title: Elevated temperature exacerbates glufosinate-ammonium-induced neurobehavioral toxicity in juvenile Eriocheir sinensis.
abstract: Under the combined pressures of global climate change and agrochemical pollution, the interactive risk of high temperature and pesticide exposure remains unclear. This 30-day chronic toxicity study systematically elucidated how high temperature exacerbates glufosinate-ammonium (GLA)-induced neurobehavioral toxicity in juvenile Eriocheir sinensis. The results showed that GLA exposure induced significant neurobehavioral abnormalities, including appendage tremors and hyperactivity, with temperature exerting non-monotonic modulation: moderate warming (26 °C) aggravated excitatory behaviors, while extreme high temperature (30 °C) inhibited locomotion due to exceeding physiological tolerance thresholds, reflecting nervous system failure rather than recovery. Mechanistically, high temperature potentiated GLA-induced oxidative stress, triggering the "oxidative stress-neuroinflammation-apoptosis" cascade which ultimately led to neurocyte apoptosis or neuronal damage, as validated by increased serum levels of neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and central nervous system specific protein β (S100β). Targeted metabolomics revealed that combined stress disrupted neurotransmitter homeostasis. Excitatory neurotransmitters L-glutamic acid and L-aspartic acid were significantly increased, inducing excitotoxicity, while compensatory GABA elevation failed to reverse neural excitation-inhibition imbalance. This study is the first to reveal the multi-pathway, multi-organ coordinated mechanism by which high temperature amplifies GLA's neurobehavioral toxicity, providing a critical scientific basis for pesticide ecological risk assessment under global warming.

title: Mechanisms of first- to fourth-generation neonicotinoid resistance in Myzus persicae from Beijing peach orchards: Roles of target-site mutations and detoxification metabolism.
abstract: Myzus persicae is a globally destructive pest that has evolved severe resistance to neonicotinoids. However, the resistance status and underlying mechanisms in peach orchards of Beijing, China remain largely unknown. In this study, the resistance of six field populations collected from Beijing peach orchards against five neonicotinoids (representing first- to fourth-generation compounds) was investigated, and the molecular mechanisms were elucidated. Bioassays revealed resistance to imidacloprid (15.99-30.97-fold), acetamiprid (9.16-50.79-fold), sulfoxaflor (1.28-25.26-fold), thiamethoxam (6.12-16.95-fold), and dinotefuran (6.63-12.27-fold) across these populations. Mutation screening identified the known R81T and V101I mutations, along with a novel R81S substitution in the nAChR β1 subunit. Genotyping indicated that V101I single mutations were predominant (69.75% of individuals), while R81T/S + V101I combination mutations were detected in 22.56% of individuals. The results revealed that the R81T/S + V101I combination mutations confer substantially higher resistance (73.10->1146.79-fold) than V101I alone (13.73-394.21-fold) using monoclonal strains. Enzyme activity assays demonstrated that elevated P450 (1.18-1.56-fold), GST (1.32-2.18-fold), and CarE (1.64-2.59-fold) activities are associated with neonicotinoid resistance across all genotype backgrounds, with PBO showing the strongest synergistic effects (synergism ratios: 1.39-7.90). TPP and DEM exhibited synergism ratios ranging from 0.69 to 3.10. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that all mutations altered nAChR binding-pocket geometry, with combination mutations causing more pronounced structural perturbations and reduced imidacloprid binding affinity than V101I alone. These findings show that target-site mutations and detoxification enzymes act concertedly to drive neonicotinoid resistance in M. persicae, highlighting the need for insecticide rotation for sustainable management.

title: Using brain age algorithms to understand physical activity's impact on MS.
Multimodal Neuroimaging and Behavioral Characterization of Aged Female APOE4 Knock-In Rats Reveals a Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease Phenotype.
abstract: The apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (APOE4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease (AD) and confers disproportionate risk in women, particularly after reproductive senescence. The brain changes preceding overt neurodegeneration in APOE4 carriers remain incompletely characterized. We conducted neuroimaging and behavioral studies in aged (18-month) female APOE4 humanized knock-in rats and APOE3 controls. Regional brain volumes across 197 areas were quantified by voxel-based morphometry (VBM); white and gray matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), yielding fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Spatial memory was assessed with the Barnes maze and motor coordination with the beam walk. APOE4 rats showed significantly larger regional brain volumes than APOE3 controls. DTI revealed increased FA in the thalamus, brainstem, and white matter tracts, and reduced FA in the sensorimotor cortex. Across most regions elevated FA was accompanied by reduced ADC, an inverse relationship consistent with cytotoxic edema. Behaviorally, APOE4 rats were significantly impaired on the Barnes maze. Aged female APOE4 knock-in rats exhibit a preclinical AD phenotype: widespread volumetric enlargement across white matter, sensorimotor, and limbic circuits, with microstructural alterations (elevated FA in brainstem, thalamus, and white matter; reduced FA in sensorimotor cortex). This mirrors the imaging and cognitive profile of cognitively normal human APOE4 carriers in preclinical AD and validates the model as a translationally relevant platform for investigating early APOE4-driven pathophysiology and testing preventive interventions.

title: Engineering a Bioelectronic Hybrid Heart with Integrated Sensing and Electrical Modulation.
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide, motivating the development of advanced therapeutic strategies, including engineered cardiac substitutes. Here, we report a bioelectronic hybrid heart that integrates engineered cardiac tissue with embedded electrophysiological sensing and stimulation capabilities. A decellularized cardiac scaffold was cellularized by injection of induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes and assembled with a cell-laden, three-dimensional-printed extracellular matrix coating containing a custom-designed electronic mesh. After 14 days of culture, the embedded electrodes recorded spontaneous cardiac activity, while localized electrical stimulation affected the tissue, enabling pacing at controlled frequencies. Calcium imaging demonstrated spatial activation across the engineered tissue during pacing. This platform establishes a foundation for integrating real-time monitoring and electronic functional regulation into engineered cardiac constructs and represents an initial step toward bioelectronic organ engineering.

title: Single cell landscape of sex differences in the different courses of multiple sclerosis.
abstract: One of the major challenges in addressing multiple sclerosis is to understand its progression trajectory. The pathological process transitions from acute phases predominantly driven by inflammation to progressive clinical profiles where neurodegeneration takes precedence. It is known that sex plays a crucial role in this heterogeneity; females are two to three times more likely to suffer from multiple sclerosis, while males suffer from more rapid neurodegeneration with greater severity. To gain insight into the sex-based molecular differences, we processed single cell datasets from the central nervous system and the peripheral blood, covering the different courses of multiple sclerosis. We generated cell-type specific landscapes, including gene signatures from differentially expressed genes, functional profiling, pathway activation, and cell-cell communication networks for females, males, and their sex differential profiles. Among our findings, we revealed that female neurons may exhibit protective mechanisms against neurodegeneration. In the inflammatory-predominant forms, female immune cells present an inflammatory core driven by the AP-1 transcription factor, while male adaptive immune cells exhibit higher mitochondrial impairment. Conversely, larger differences are reported in CD8 + T cells progressive forms, with males exhibiting cytolytic profiles that may promote neurodegeneration. Complete results can be explored in the interactive webtool https://irsoler.shinyapps.io/cbl-atlas-ms/ . We identified cell-type specific sex differences in brain and immune cells that vary in the spectrum of multiple sclerosis. We consider this molecular description a valuable resource to promote future targeted approaches considering the sex of the individual.

title: Randomized pilot trial of intraoperative hemoadsorption in clopidogrel treated patients undergoing urgent coronary artery bypass grafting.
abstract: Patients receiving clopidogrel who undergo urgent CABG before the recommended 5-day washout period are at increased risk of perioperative bleeding. This study evaluated whether intraoperative hemoadsorption can reduce bleeding in such patients. Patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of clopidogrel discontinuation were randomized 1:1 to intraoperative hemoadsorption (Group 1) or control (Group 2). In the intervention group, the device was incorporated into the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuit. Efficacy was assessed by 24-hour chest tube drainage (CTD), blood product transfusions and surgical revisions for bleeding control. A total of 50 patients were randomized (mean age 64 ± 8.6 years, 82% male). There were no differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Group 1 showed significantly reduced median 24-hr CTD of 300mL [250-400] vs. 500mL [400-700], p = 0.0003, transfusions of packed red blood cells 0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-2] units, p = 0.047), fresh frozen plasma 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [2-3] units, p < 0.0001) and platelets 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [1-3] units, p < 0.0001 compared with Group 2. One revision for bleeding control occurred in Group 2 (4.0%). No device-related serious adverse events were observed. In this cohort of clopidogrel-treated patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of discontinuation, intraoperative hemoadsorption was associated with lower postoperative bleeding and transfusion requirements.

title: Blood-brain barrier and blood-tumoral barrier formation in glioblastoma: endothelial cells and glioblastoma stem cells at the immune-brain crossroad.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by significant cellular and molecular complexity. Central to this complexity are glioma stem cells (GSCs) and the perivascular niche, a specialized microenvironment that integrates signals from the systemic circulation with cues arising from tumor development. Acting as a regulatory hub, the perivascular niche influences GSC proliferation, migration, and resistance to therapy through multiple interactions among vascular, immune, and tumor cell populations. In this review, we focus on GSCs and examine the cellular composition and molecular mechanisms operating within the perivascular niche, highlighting key modes of crosstalk that sustain tumor progression. We furthermore critically evaluate experimental strategies used to study this compartment, including 2D and 3D cell cultures, organoids, and in vivo models, discussing their respective strengths and limitations for testing intercellular interactions and therapeutic approaches. A comprehensive understanding of tumor heterogeneity and the interactions between different tumor cell populations, combined with well-characterized experimental models, is essential for deriving mechanistic insights and informing the development of more effective targeted therapies for GBM, ultimately advancing our knowledge of how tumor-microenvironment interactions drive GBM progression.

title: Treatment interventions for co-occurring opioid use disorder, and sleep disturbances: a scoping review.
journal: Substance abuse treatment, prevention, and policy
abstract: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is part of the broader spectrum of substance use disorders often complicated by psychiatric symptoms such as depression, anxiety, PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder), and sleep disturbances, with insomnia being particularly frequent. These psychiatric symptoms may act as precipitating factors and consequences of OUD, reinforcing a complex bidirectional relationship that complicates treatment and recovery. Despite the clinical importance of dual disorders, sleep impairments are particularly relevant yet understudied therapeutic targets and literature addressing sleep disturbances in the context of psychiatric symptoms or disorders in OUD remains limited. This scoping review examines pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions of OUD and sleep disturbances in the presence of psychiatric disorders or symptoms, such as anxiety, depression, and PTSD. This review follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines using the following keywords: ("sleep" OR "insomnia") AND ("depression" OR "anxiety" OR "PTSD" OR "post-traumatic stress disorder" OR "posttraumatic stress disorder") AND ("opioid use disorder" OR "OUD" OR "opioid addiction. Sleep disordered breathing was excluded. Participants were adults (> 18 years old) with OUD or opioid dependence undergoing withdrawal or treatment. The study focused on quantitative and qualitative study designs. Fifteen studies including 1,167 adults with OUD or opioid dependence were selected and categorized into pharmacological (targeting opioid or non-opioid receptors) and non-pharmacological interventions. Most interventions were adjunctive to opioid substitution or antagonist therapies. Naltrexone-induced insomnia was common but did not significantly affect mood and could be mitigated with lorazepam. Non-opioid pharmacotherapies yielded mixed results: guanfacine is suggested to increase insomnia risk but reduce stress and craving, while amitriptyline, prazepam, dronabinol, and neurotransmitter-precursor-supplements showed potential in improving sleep and withdrawal symptoms. Improved characterization and management of impaired sleep in individuals with OUD and psychiatric symptoms may reduce relapse risk, enhance emotional regulation, and decrease self-medication. Clinicians should consider the complex interplay between OUD, psychiatric symptoms, and sleep as part of comprehensive care. Further research is needed to clarify these interactions and support the development of integrated, evidence-based strategies for treatment and prevention. Not applicable.

title: Gait environments recognition via synaptic convolutional neural network with memory autapses.
abstract: Exoskeleton systems face significant challenges in maintaining reliable gait prediction under dynamically changing walking environments. Conventional learning-based methods often suffer from limited adaptability and high computational latency, especially when deployed on low-power embedded hardware. A neuromorphic computing framework based on a synaptic convolutional neural network with memory autapses (SCN-MA) is introduced for real-time gait environment recognition. A structured gait experiment was conducted to collect pneumatic mechanomyography (pMMG) and stretch signals under multiple walking conditions, forming a multimodal dataset for training and evaluation. The framework adopts multiple binary gait classification models trained in parallel, which enhances modularity and scalability. A reinforcement learning based ensemble policy is then trained to integrate the outputs of these models for final decision-making. The complete system is implemented on the Zynq-based FPGA platform, enabling end-to-end prediction with low latency and high energy efficiency. Experimental results confirm improved accuracy and adaptability over baseline models, supporting the use of neuromorphic architectures in exoskeleton systems.

title: Near-infrared-activated CuTA@PDA@PTH nanozymes remodel the osteoarthritic microenvironment for coordinated cartilage protection and subchondral bone repair.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive whole-joint disorder involving cartilage degeneration, oxidative stress, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Current treatments mainly provide symptomatic relief and rarely restore joint microenvironmental homeostasis. Here, we developed a multifunctional near-infrared (NIR)-responsive CuTA@PDA@PTH nanozyme, termed CPP, for OA therapy. CPP was constructed through copper-tannic acid coordination, polydopamine coating, and PTH 1-34 incorporation, integrating antioxidant catalytic activity, photothermal responsiveness, and peptide-mediated bioactivity. CPP exhibited uniform morphology, good dispersibility, stable photothermal behavior, and broad-spectrum ROS-scavenging activity with SOD-like and CAT-like functions. In vitro, NIR-activated CPP reduced H₂O₂-induced ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis in chondrocytes, while promoting proliferation and restoring cartilage matrix homeostasis. CPP-NIR also downregulated inflammatory and catabolic markers, attenuated M1-associated activation, favored an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype, and enhanced BMSC migration and osteogenic differentiation under oxidative stress. In a DMM-induced mouse OA model, intra-articular CPP combined with NIR irradiation prolonged joint retention, attenuated cartilage degeneration, reduced osteophyte formation, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and alleviated synovial inflammation. These findings support NIR-activated CPP as a multi-axis nanozyme platform for redox, immune, cartilage, and subchondral bone microenvironment regulation in OA.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in microglia: a novel perspective of depression pathogenesis.
abstract: Major depressive disorder is a prevalent psychiatric disease that is closely linked to chronic low-grade neuroinflammation, which is primarily driven by microglia, the primary resident immune cells in the brain. Accumulating studies started to reveal that mitochondria, the powerhouses of the cell, play an important role in microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and neurotoxicity in depression. Stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction triggers microglial activation through distinct mechanisms including energy metabolism patterns transition, electron transport chain impairment, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial DNA damage, imbalanced fission and fusion, autophagy, and mitophagy deficiency, which cause the onset and progression of depression. In this review, we described microglial activation in animal models and clinically depressed patients, summarized current understanding of mitochondrial dysfunction-mediated microglial activation, and emphasized the possible mechanisms by which microglial mitochondrial dysfunction participates in the pathogenesis of depression. Understanding the roles and underlying mechanisms of mitochondrial dysfunction in neuroinflammation and neurotoxicity in depression may shed light on developing novel therapeutic strategies to fight against this devastating mental illness.

title: Current situation and influencing factors of knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to depression among parents of adolescents with depression.
abstract: To assess depression-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among parents of adolescents hospitalized with depression and to identify associated factors. Using purposive sampling, we surveyed 138 parents of adolescents with depression hospitalized at our center (December 2023-September 2024). Participants completed a 25-item questionnaire covering knowledge (10 items), attitudes (9 items), and practices (6 items). Group differences were examined using independent-samples t tests or one-way ANOVA (with appropriate nonparametric tests when assumptions were not met). Multiple linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with KAP (overall and by subdomain). Mean standardized scores (0-100) were 54.33 ± 13.59 for knowledge, 59.29 ± 10.93 for attitudes, 73.77 ± 12.20 for practices, and 60.78 ± 7.46 overall. Knowledge, attitudes, and overall scores differed by age, occupation, and education. Knowledge, practices, and overall scores differed by education, monthly income, and residence. In multivariable models, age, occupation, education, and income were independently associated with the overall KAP score (all p < 0.05). Parents of adolescents with depression demonstrated limited disease-related knowledge, comparatively negative attitudes, and moderate practices. These findings highlight the need for targeted psychoeducation and support to improve parental mental health literacy in the inpatient setting.

title: The impact of pain neuroscience education on physical therapy students' pain knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, and clinical recommendations: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Pain neuroscience education (PNE) promotes a biopsychosocial understanding of pain among health-professional students, yet evidence for its long-term effects outside high-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated the immediate and six-month effects of a single PNE lecture on pain knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, and clinical recommendations in Jordanian physiotherapy students. A parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted with first- and second-year physiotherapy students. Students were randomized (1:1; 60 per group) to a 70-minute PNE lecture or an attention-matched musculoskeletal red flags lecture. Primary outcomes were pain knowledge (Revised Neurophysiology of Pain Questionnaire [RNPQ]) and pain-related attitudes (modified Health Care Providers' Pain and Impairment Relationship Scale [HC-PAIRS]). The secondary outcome was guideline-concordant recommendations assessed using a validated vignette. Analyses included linear and logistic mixed-effects models, with responder analyses using minimal clinically important difference thresholds to estimate numbers needed to treat (NNTs). All students (N = 120) completed the study with no attrition. Significant group × time interactions were observed for pain knowledge and attitudes (both p 0.05). Responder analyses demonstrated substantial immediate educational benefit (NNT 2.7 for knowledge, 3.6 for attitudes), which decreased at six months, consistent with attenuation of intervention effects over time. A single 70-minute PNE session produced significant and clinically meaningful immediate improvements in pain knowledge, attitudes, and guideline-concordant clinical recommendations. At six months, pain knowledge remained significantly improved, whereas the remaining effects attenuated. These findings support consideration of embedding PNE early within pre-licensure physiotherapy curricula. Future research should determine whether recursive reinforcement improves longer-term retention of educational gains. The study protocol was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06821022) on February 6, 2025.

title: Everyday struggles to stay healthy: experiences of people at high risk of stroke residing in low socioeconomic urban neighbourhoods in Stockholm.
abstract: Residents in low socioeconomic urban neighbourhoods are disproportionately exposed to modifiable risk factors, yet their engagement in health-promoting behaviours remains poorly understood from a lived experience perspective. This study aims to explore how residents at high risk of stroke experience and engage in everyday health-promoting activities within their neighbourhoods. A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with eighteen adults residing in low socioeconomic urban neighbourhoods in Sweden who were identified as being at high risk of stroke. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, following Braun and Clarke's approach, to capture participants' experiences at multiple levels. Three themes were developed: When caring for others becomes a barrier to one's own health, When economic conditions hinder engagement in health-promoting behaviours, and When health-promoting spaces become stressful and unsafe. Participants described how caregiving responsibilities, financial constraints, and stress limited their capacity to engage in health-promoting activities. Although participants often had knowledge of healthy behaviours and expressed motivation, their efforts were disrupted by competing demands and constrained life conditions. Spaces typically framed as supportive of health, such as gyms, were not always experienced as accessible and could instead evoke discomfort, stress, or insecurity. Social support was present but often insufficient to overcome these cumulative challenges. Engagement in health-promoting activities among individuals in low socioeconomic urban contexts is shaped by the intersection of relational, structural, and contextual factors, rather than by individual motivation alone. Health promotion may be experienced as an additional burden within already constrained lives. Effective health promotion strategies should therefore move beyond individual behaviour change and adopt context-sensitive, multi-level approaches that are integrated into everyday life by fostering meaningful and varied forms of engagement. Such approaches are essential to reach and ensure the active participation of residents of low socioeconomic areas in health-promoting initiatives. Not applicable.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of CSF tap-test parameters in predicting shunt responsiveness in normal pressure hydrocephalus: a cohort study.
abstract: The cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CSF-TT) is widely used as an ancillary test to select patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) for ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt surgery; however, its diagnostic utility remains unclear. To evaluate the diagnostic utility of CSF-TT in predicting outcomes following VP shunts. Patients with probable iNPH underwent assessments of gait, urinary, and cognitive function using the Dutch gait scale, timed up and go (TUG) gait score, iNPH grading scale, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at baseline and 24 h after CSF-TT. They were offered VP shunt surgery based on the clinico-radiological profile, regardless of CSF-TT outcome. Postoperative outcomes were evaluated at 24 weeks, and patients who showed ≥ 1-point improvement in mRS were classified as shunt responders. We also assessed the diagnostic accuracy of the tap test for predicting ≥ 1-point improvement in iNPH at 24 weeks. The diagnostic performance of various baseline tests was assessed using the area under receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs). 24 patients underwent VP shunting, 15 (62.5%) were classified as shunt responders. A one-point reduction in the mRS at 24 h post-CSF-TT had a sensitivity of 53.3% (95% CI: 26.6-78.7) and specificity of 66.7% (95% CI: 29.9-92.5) in predicting shunt responsiveness based on mRS as outcome. A one-point reduction in the iNPH scale at 24 h post CSF-TT had a sensitivity of 64.3% (95%CI 35.1-87.2) and a specificity of 66.7% (95% CI 22.3-95.7) to predict a one-point improvement in the iNPH scale at 24 weeks post VP shunt. Changes in mRS, Dutch gait score, TUG test score, and iNPH score were not valid predictors, as the confidence intervals of the AUROCs crossed 0.5. CSF-TT parameters show limited accuracy in predicting shunt responsiveness in patients with iNPH. Our results suggest that about one-third of positive tap tests were false positives, and the test has poor diagnostic performance as a standalone predictor of postoperative shunt outcomes.

title: TIRELESS study protocol: non-inferiority study of nurse-led web-based cognitive behavioral therapy for cancer-related fatigue in patients with incurable cancer.
authors: van der Rijt Carin C D
van der Vorst Maurice J D L
abstract: Fatigue is a prevalent and debilitating symptom for patients with incurable cancer. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can significantly reduce cancer-related fatigue in this patient group. However, implementation of CBT into clinical care is difficult as the intervention is time-intensive, costly, and requires face-to-face consultations with a specialized CBT therapist. Since nurses already support patient with symptom management, including fatigue, internet supported CBT delivered by nurses could be a promising alternative for patients with incurable cancer. The primary aim of this study is to determine the non-inferiority of nurse-led web-based CBT in its effect on cancer-related fatigue, compared to CBT provided by CBT therapists. The study is a prospective, non-randomized study using historical cohorts as the benchmark for comparison. Severely fatigued patients with incurable cancer of a solid tumor receive a 12-week nurse-led web-based CBT intervention. Primary and secondary outcome measures are assessed at baseline, post-intervention (14 weeks), and follow-up (26 weeks). The primary outcome measure is fatigue severity assessed with the Checklist Individual Strength (CIS-subscale fatigue severity). Secondary outcomes include functional impairment, quality of life and fatigue assessed with EORTC-QLQ-C30, and health care costs. Primary and secondary outcomes of the TIRELESS study and the benchmark are compared to determine non-inferiority. Non-inferiority of fatigue reduction is concluded if the upper bound of the one-sided 95% CI does not exceed + 5 on the CIS, with higher scores indicating more severe fatigue. In addition, interviews are conducted to gain insight in nurses' and patients' experiences with the intervention. These data are analyzed applying a thematic analysis method. Recruitment has started in June 2024. Especially for this burdened patient group, integration of CBT for fatigue in routine medical care is essential. With the TIRELESS study, we aim to reduce patient burden, foster scalability and accessibility of CBT for fatigue, and increase patients' self-management. If this approach is non-inferior to the original evidence-based (benchmark) intervention, this will enable implementation of cancer-related fatigue interventions for the growing group of patients with incurable cancer. NCT06511518; date of registration: 23/02/2024.

title: Diagnosis of a chiasmal lesion compressing optic chiasm in patients with severe retinal degeneration: a two-case report.
abstract: Optic chiasmal compression is an important cause of progressive visual dysfunction, and early diagnosis is essential to prevent irreversible vision loss. However, recognition can be delayed when patients have pre-existing ocular diseases that independently impair vision. Severe retinal degeneration may obscure the clinical signs of chiasmal compression and complicate diagnostic evaluation. Here, we report two elderly patients with advanced retinal degeneration in whom pituitary tumors compressing the optic chiasm were initially unrecognized, highlighting important diagnostic challenges and clinical considerations for improving diagnostic accuracy. Case 1: An 84-year-old woman presented with a three-year history of progressively worsening visual field defects and blurred vision. She had been under regular follow-up and treatment for longstanding polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy in the right eye and central serous chorioretinopathy in the left eye. Although fundus examination and optical coherence tomography demonstrated advanced macular changes, these findings were considered insufficient to fully explain the degree of visual decline. Visual field testing, performed to evaluate her subjective visual disturbance, revealed bitemporal hemianopia. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a large pituitary adenoma compressing the optic chiasm. Case 2: A 79-year-old man with severe myopic degeneration and pre-existing low vision presented with unexplained progressive visual decline over 1.5 years. Although fundus examination demonstrated advanced myopic changes, the severity and progression of visual loss were not fully explained by the underlying retinal findings. At initial presentation, a relative afferent pupillary defect was noted in the right eye, prompting further evaluation. Visual field testing and neuroimaging were performed at the initial visit. MRI revealed a pituitary adenoma extending into the suprasellar region with optic chiasmal compression. Optic chiasmal compression should be considered in patients with severe retinal degeneration presenting with progressive visual decline that cannot be fully explained by retinal pathology. Visual field testing and timely neuroimaging, particularly MRI, are essential for accurate diagnosis and may help prevent irreversible visual loss.

title: EIF3B is associated with m6A-related regulation of E2F7 and promotes stemness in glioblastoma multiforme.
abstract: E2F transcription factors are key regulators of the cell cycle and play an important role in tumorigenesis. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic cells, is also crucial for cancer progression. However, the interplay between E2F family members and m6A modification in glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) remains poorly understood. We applied weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify m6A-related gene modules co-expressed with E2F7, a gene that is significantly associated with adverse prognosis and tumor stemness. Through intersection analysis, eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit B (EIF3B) emerged as a hub gene, showing a strong positive correlation with E2F7 in GBM datasets. Functional validation was performed in GBM cells to assess the regulatory relationship between EIF3B and E2F7, including examination of mRNA and protein expression, mRNA stability, and m6A modification levels. GBM stemness was evaluated by tumor sphere formation assays and detection of stemness-associated markers. Functional validation revealed that EIF3B knockdown reduced E2F7 mRNA and protein expression, promoted E2F7 mRNA degradation, and decreased its m6A modification, suggesting an association between EIF3B and m6A-related regulation of E2F7 stability. Furthermore, EIF3B knockdown markedly suppressed GBM stemness, as demonstrated by impaired tumor sphere formation and downregulation of stemness-associated markers. Clinically, EIF3B expression increased with glioma grade and correlated with poor prognosis. Collectively, these findings suggest that the EIF3B-E2F7 axis is associated with m6A-related regulation in GBM and may warrant further investigation as a candidate for therapeutic targeting.

title: Evaluating 16S metagenomics data analysis pipelines using an Ion Torrent sequencer for human gut microbiome research.
abstract: High-throughput 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing is essential for characterizing gut dysbiosis in translational research. However, microbiome profiles vary widely across sequencing platforms, library preparation protocols, targeted hypervariable regions (HVRs), and bioinformatics workflows. For users of the Ion Torrent S5 platform, there is currently no consensus methodology for performing open-source analyses as an alternative to proprietary frameworks. This study evaluates the proprietary Ion Reporter™ software against eight open-source pipelines based on QIIME2 and the SILVA database, accounting for data compositionality. Benchmarking was performed using a commercial human fecal reference material (ZymoBIOMICS™ D6323) characterized via DNA-shotgun sequencing (the ZB-Shotgun profile), as the reference standard. Poisson regression modeling showed that using two primer sets for library preparation yielded a 30 % lower expected read count than a single primer set (IRR = 0.6986, p < 0.001). Across all configurations, the choice of denoising algorithm (DADA2 vs. Deblur) significantly affected alpha diversity calculations. At the phylum level, hierarchical clustering of Bayes factors (BFs) indicated that multi-region Ion Reporter workflows produced stable consensus predictions. Conversely, at the species level, single-HVR open-source pipelines significantly outperformed multi-region approaches. Open-source pipelines that combine targeted HVR2 or HVR4 inputs with state-of-the-art denoisers outperform proprietary Ion Reporter options, providing superior taxonomic resolution and precision for species-level microbiome profiling. This study establishes a traceable, reproducible, and cost-effective framework that empowers independent researchers to maximize the utility of Ion Torrent 16S rRNA data in healthcare and gastrointestinal research without relying on restrictive software ecosystems.

title: RBFOX3 is associated with neuronal-like phenotypic transition in recurrent glioblastoma.
abstract: Emerging evidence links neuronal-like phenotypic transition to glioblastoma (GB) recurrence and therapy resistance, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that dysregulated alternative splicing leads to a neuronal-like state and chemoresistance at tumor recurrence. We reanalysed longitudinal bulk RNA-seq data from paired primary and recurrent GBs to quantify dynamic alternative splicing during tumor evolution. By integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we characterized shifts in cellular composition and spatial interactions linked to these splicing changes. We then prioritized splicing regulators and validated their effects on tumor cells using in vitro cell lines and co-culture assays. A subset of recurrent GBs exhibits neuronal programs and chemoresistance during tumor evolution, accompanied by pronounced differential splicing patterns. Single-cell analyses link these splicing changes to the co-enrichment of neurons and a neuronal-like tumor subpopulation at recurrence. Spatial transcriptomics further indicates close synaptic interactions between this tumor state and adjacent neurons in tumor-infiltrative regions. Through integrative computational ranking and experimental validation, we find that the neuron-specific splicing factor RBFOX3 promotes the neuronal-like GB tumor state by dysregulating splicing. In tumor-neuron co-culture systems, RBFOX3 overexpression is linked to the upregulation of presynaptic markers. Dysregulated alternative splicing mediated by RBFOX3 is associated with a neuronal-like tumor state and might contribute to chemoresistance at GB relapse, highlighting the potential role of splicing regulation in GB evolution.

title: Decoding Formulation Complexity: Comparative Performance of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence Models in Intelligent Nano Depot (iNDEP) Design.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly explored to improve predictive modelling and optimization in pharmaceutical formulation development. This study compared predictive performance of conventional statistical approaches and AI/ML-based models using an experimentally generated dataset from PLGA-mPEG-based Intelligent Nano Depot (iNDEP), smart depot forming long-acting injectable system for sustained co-delivery of Memantine hydrochloride (MH) and Galantamine hydrobromide (GH). Central Composite Design (CCD) dataset of 17 experimental formulations were employed to develop predictive models. The % cumulative drug release (CDR), implant formation time and particle size were measured to determine effects of PLGA-mPEG, Span 80 and Tween 80. Design of Experiments (DoE), SPSS-based Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and ML workflows in Orange Data Mining and KNIME Analytics Platform were used to produce predictive models. Root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) were used to evaluate model performance. Models developed using DoE were good fit with R2 values ranging from 0.9882 to 0.9916. The MLR models predicted perfectly (R2 = 0.866-0.951) for the %CDR responses using SPSS. ANN models successfully captured nonlinear relationships between formulation and response. Analysis of ML workflows indicated varying performance of algorithms depending on response; there was no one model that performed good across all responses. Traditional statistical and AI-based predictive methods complement each other. The integration of DoE with AI- and ML-based modelling offers a comprehensive tool for enhancing prediction accuracy and guiding formulation and optimization of pharmaceutical products.

title: PLGA-Phospholipid Hybrid Oleogel In Situ Forming Implant for Sustained 30-Day Co-Delivery of Dosnepezil and Memantine.
abstract: The management of Alzheimer's disease requires continuous therapeutic intervention due to its progressive nature. Currently, the FDA has approved acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA receptor antagonists, and disease-modifying monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease. This study aimed to develop a long-acting injectable formulation for symptomatic therapy. An in-situ gel formulation, DM00PG-M13, comprising Lipoid, PLGA (50:50), and sesame oil, was developed and loaded with memantine and donepezil for combination therapy. The optimized gel formulation demonstrated good uniformity with a pH of 7.80 ± 0.015. Rheological and syringeability studies showed a consistent viscosity in the range of 0.20-0.22 Pa·s and an injection force of 9.97 ± 0.29 N using a 22-G needle. In vitro drug release studies performed in phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4) demonstrated sustained drug release over one month, with cumulative releases of 82.58% for donepezil and 87.61% for memantine after 30 days. Furthermore, the release kinetics were best described by the Peppas-Sahlin model for donepezil and the Weibull-lag model for memantine. Ex vivo studies evaluating the optimized formulation injected into pig muscle tissue showed release profiles comparable to the in vitro release pattern, with approximately 20% release of donepezil and 26% release of memantine over 7 days, indicating sustained release behavior. Cytotoxicity studies using NIH/3T3 fibroblast cells confirmed the formulation's safety profile. Overall, these results suggest that the drug-loaded DM00PG-M13 formulation can be administered intramuscularly as a depot system for sustained drug release, potentially improving patient compliance.

title: Gut-brain axis in Alzheimer's disease: neuroinflammatory mechanisms and immunopharmacological interventions.
abstract: Despite being defined pathologically by amyloid-β plaques, chronic neuroinflammation and neurofibrillary tangles, the drugs that target these processes directly (lecanemab and donanemab) have only modest effects on the clinical course of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and significant safety concerns have been identified, so there is renewed interest in upstream, systemic contributors to disease. This review aims to provide a synthesis of the latest mechanistic and clinical evidence that gut microbiota dysbiosis is associated with Alzheimer's disease with a specifically immunopharmacological focus. We will explore how the gut-brain axis pathways (vagal, immune, endocrine and microbial-metabolite signaling) converge to trigger microglial and astrocytic activation via toll-like receptor 4/NF-κB and complement-primed NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, which is also directly activated by amyloid-β and tau. Then we review the immunopharmacological interventions intended to break this axis - probiotic supplementation (some consistent benefit - although mild) and sodium oligomannate, with strong preclinical and case report signals that need human trials (in 2026) and polyphenols and GLP-1 receptor agonists, which have a persistent disconnect between mechanistic promise and clinical efficacy, including a definitive null result for semaglutide in 2026. Translative directions are addressed to nanotechnology-based delivery systems for improving bioavailability and blood-brain barrier penetration, as well as emerging precision-medicine, AI-driven approaches in the selection of treatments based on microbiome information. It is our opinion that because the gut-brain-immune axis is a mechanistically supported and potentially highly scalable therapeutic target, complementary to amyloid and tau therapies, the development of future therapies should match the inflammatory, metabolic and microbial phenotypes.

title: Correction: Mast Cells in Neuroimmune Interactions: Mechanisms, Pathophysiological Roles, and Therapeutic Implications.
Clinical heterogeneity in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy: data-driven subtypes challenge current classification.
abstract: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) presents with substantial phenotypic heterogeneity, yet current classifications do not adequately capture clinically meaningful subgroups. Thus, we aimed to discover novel, clinically meaningful CIDP subgroups using unbiased clustering. In this observational, multicenter retrospective cohort study we screened 425 patients diagnosed with typical CIDP or CIDP variants from 10 German centers. Standardized data including demographic, clinical, electrophysiological, laboratory, comorbidity, and treatment information were collected. 325 patients were then randomly assigned to the discovery cohort and 100 to the validation cohort. We performed unbiased clustering and post-hoc analysis to identify clusters and define subtypes. Four distinct clusters showed marked differences: Cluster 1: Female patients with high symptom level, high disability scores, ANA positivity and autoimmune comorbidities Cluster 2: Moderate to low symptom level with low disability scores, demyelination-dominant and less comorbidities Cluster 3: High symptom level, axonal-demyelinating damage and cardiovascular comorbidities Cluster 4: Multifocal CIDP with high disability scores as well as frequent ataxia and areflexia Post hoc analyses showed marked differences in disease progression and therapeutic strategies, with clusters 1 and 4 showing particularly high rates of progression and disability. Unbiased clustering revealed four clinically meaningful CIDP subtypes, each exhibiting distinct presentations and trajectories. We identified two red flag subgroups suggesting that CIDP comprises biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease phenotypes. These findings may support more individualized monitoring and therapeutic strategies for high-risk patients and raise the possibility of distinct underlying pathomechanisms across CIDP subgroups.

title: Effect of Esketamine Pretreatment on Necroptosis in Mice with Trigeminal Neuralgia and Anxiety-Like Behavior via the RIP1/RIP3/MLKL Pathway.
abstract: To explore the effect of esketamine (ES) pretreatment on necroptosis in mice with trigeminal neuralgia accompanied by anxiety-like behavior and its correlation with the RIP1/RIP3/MLKL signaling pathway. Thirty male C57BL/6J mice were randomized into five groups (n=6): Control, Sham, model group (PIONT), PIONT+NS, and PIONT+ES. Trigeminal neuralgia model was established by left infraorbital nerve transection. ES (10 mg/kg, i.p.) was given daily for 5 days preoperatively (preoperative pretreatment) in the PIONT+ES group before molding, and equal-volume saline was administered identically in the PIONT+NS group. Pain thresholds were measured on postoperative days 3, 7, 14 and 21. Behavioral assessments were conducted on day 19, and tissue samples were harvested on day 21. Histopathological staining, immunofluorescence, qPCR, Western blot, ELISA and molecular docking were further performed for subsequent analyses. PIONT group showed reduced pain thresholds, anxiety-like behaviors, neuronal degeneration, decreased dendritic spine density, elevated TNF-α, and upregulated RIP1/RIP3/MLKL (all P<0.05). ES pretreatment prevented the development of these pathological alterations, with improved neuropathology, reduced TNF-α/RIP1/RIP3/MLKL levels, and increased spine density (P<0.05). Molecular docking showed ES binds RIP1/RIP3/MLKL/TNF-α with energies -5.46, -5.10, -5.94, -7.36 kcal/mol. ES pretreatment prevents the development of trigeminal neuralgia and anxiety-like behaviors in mice, which is associated with suppression of necroptosis-related signaling.

title: Membrane orientation regulates GAPR-1 oligomerization that is suitable for interaction with beclin 1.
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Golgi-associated plant pathogenesis-related protein 1 (GAPR-1) is a beclin 1-interacting peripheral membrane protein that is anchored to the Golgi complex via an N-myristoyl-group and ionic interactions. Here we investigated the determinants of GAPR-1 membrane binding using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and applied the results to investigate the subsequent oligomerization into biomolecular condensates and interaction with beclin 1. MD simulations revealed a specific orientation of GAPR-1 upon docking to a negatively charged lipid bilayer involving lysines at position 7 and 33 (Lys7 and Lys33). Substitution of these lysines with glutamine changed the preferred membrane orientation of GAPR-1. Upon deletion of the myristoyl-group, GAPR-1 remained docked to the lipid bilayer, but lost its preferred orientation, suggesting that myristoylation constrained the dynamics of the protein at the membrane surface. Upon mutation of Lys7 to glutamine and expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, [K7Q]GAPR-1 was prevented from myristoylation and condensate formation was severely impaired. Similar results were obtained when N-terminal myristoylation of GAPR-1 was prevented by mutating amino acid Gly2. However, in contrast to [G2A]GAPR-1, [K7Q]GAPR-1 could not interact with beclin 1 anymore upon co-expression in yeast cells, and failed to interfere with beclin 1-dependent autophagy in human cells. Our combined data show that GAPR-1 requires a defined orientation at the membrane to control protein homo-and hetero-oligomerization and to execute its function. We revealed a novel function of protein myristoylation in which it determines the motional freedom of specific protein orientations, which may have relevance for the entire myristoylated proteome.

title: Chemogenetic activation of mitochondria counteracts the Warburg effect in tumor cells.
abstract: Upregulation of glycolysis and downregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, termed as the Warburg effect, is characteristic of tumor cells. Restriction of pyruvate flux into the mitochondrial matrix is one of the major mechanisms underlying this phenomenon. Warburg metabolism is beneficial for rapidly proliferating cells; however, the metabolic consequences of activation of mitochondrial respiration in such cells remain unclear. Here we created a chemogenetic instrument, Grubraw, that generates pyruvate from ᴅ-alanine directly in the mitochondrial matrix, bypassing restricted pyruvate influx. In cancer cells, Grubraw-produced mitochondrial pyruvate increased oxidative metabolism. Chemogenetic activation of mitochondria slowed the growth rate of human melanoma xenografts. Moreover, activation of cancer cell mitochondria suppressed the transcription of genes that control cell-cycle progression, cell proliferation and DNA replication. Surprisingly, we found that cancer cells with Warburg metabolism control carbon flux by disposing of excess mitochondrial pyruvate produced by Grubraw and exporting it out of the cell.

title: Multichannel optical cochlear implants enable spectrally distinct auditory activity.
abstract: When hearing fails, cochlear implants (CIs) restore auditory perception. Yet, coding of spectral information remains a bottleneck because each electrode broadly activates the auditory nerve. As light can be more conveniently confined in space, optical (o)CIs present an alternative. Here, we combined expression of the potent channelrhodopsin ChReef in spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) with oCIs comprising 5-10 green LEDs in gerbils. This combination enabled systematic comparison of encoding intensity and spectral information by individual oCI channels to acoustic and electrical stimulation within a translationally feasible energy range. Recordings from the inferior colliculus (ICC) showed that ChReef aligned SGN light sensitivity with LED radiant fluxes: ICC activity had thresholds <200 nJ and reached a maximum equivalent to that achieved with 51 dB SPL pure tones. Multichannel oCIs enabled tonotopically ordered, spectrally distinct stimulation that more closely resembled acoustic stimulation than did electrical stimulation. Some LEDs elicited multiple spectral peaks at higher intensities. Linear discriminant analysis of ICC activity indicated improved channel discriminability for optical over electrical stimulation. In summary, µJ-oCI-stimulation achieves improved spectral resolution over state-of-the-art electrical stimulation.

title: [Artificial intelligence in the early detection of psychotic disorders: opportunities and limitations of clinical implementation].
abstract: Early detection of psychotic disorders is complicated by nonspecific symptoms, heterogeneous trajectories and the limited ability of established clinical instruments to generate accurate individual-level predictions. Data-driven artificial intelligence can integrate complex clinical and biological data and achieves moderate to good predictive performance, which often declines on external validation. Despite substantial methodological advances, a marked translational gap between model development and clinical application persists, mainly due to limited generalizability as well as practical, ethical and regulatory requirements. Artificial intelligence can complement clinical expertise and facilitate access to appropriate psychiatric care provided that it is implemented transparently and close to real-world care, subject to health economic evaluation and developed with the active involvement of experts by experience.

title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex.
abstract: Flexible cognition requires the brain to generalize across tasks while preserving task-specific information. Previous work showed that task representations are compressed in the association cortex and expanded in sensory and motor systems, but the mechanisms underlying these transformations are unclear. Here we test whether the geometry of intrinsic brain connectivity constrains how representations change between cortical regions. We analyzed functional MRI acquired during 16 diverse cognitive tasks together with activity flow modeling, finding that connectivity dimensionality predicts representational changes across the cortex. Low-dimensional connectivity compressed task representations and increased similarities across tasks, whereas high-dimensional connectivity expanded representations and supported conjunctive coding of task features. Activity flow modeling reproduced the observed compression-to-expansion pattern along the sensory-association-motor hierarchy and generated representational geometries that more closely matched targets than sources, consistent with transformation rather than transfer of information. These findings identify network geometry as a systems-level principle that shapes cortical representations and supports flexible cognition.

title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation.
abstract: Somatosensation is mediated by dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, which convert physical and chemical stimuli into electrical signals. However, the full repertoire of molecular components underlying somatosensation remains incompletely identified. Here we developed an efficient postnatal CRISPR-Cas9 knockout platform for interrogating DRG-expressed genes (such as Piezo2, Trpv1 and Scn9a) in mice using AAV9-mediated single-guide RNA delivery. Combining this approach with somatosensory behavioral assays, we performed a targeted screen of 20 genes and identified Creld1 as a cross-model regulator of somatosensation. Either single-guide RNA-mediated postnatal knockout or tamoxifen-induced Cre-mediated deletion of Creld1 in DRG neurons resulted in profound behavioral deficits in touch, temperature, pain and itch, whereas its overexpression enhanced touch and thermal responses. Mechanistically, CRELD1 functions as an auxiliary regulator of voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav) for controlling DRG neuron excitability. Together, this work establishes a robust postnatal screening platform for behavioral genomics and identifies Creld1 as a master regulator of somatosensory function.

title: Molecular functions, cellular responses and pathological implications of the RNA modification N6-methyladenosine.
abstract: The RNA modification N6-methyladenosine (m6A) precisely regulates eukaryotic gene expression. The deposition of m6A is governed by chromatin environment, transcription and RNA processing. m6A modifications influence chromatin function and RNA splicing, stability, localization and translation, and enable cellular adaptation to environmental changes. Dysregulation of m6A has been implicated in pathological processes, including neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. In this Review, we dissect the m6A machinery by describing how writers and erasers coordinate m6A deposition and reader proteins translate these modifications into diverse functional outcomes. We illustrate how this dynamic regulatory network orchestrates cellular stress responses, metabolic homeostasis and antitumour immunity, and outline the pathological consequences of m6A dysregulation in brain disorders and cancer. Finally, we highlight translational prospects of m6A biology, including the development of specific small-molecule inhibitors and precise editing technologies, and address the remaining challenges for clinical interventions targeting m6A.

title: In vivo replication of a fully functional nerve net in a clonally reproducing animal.
abstract: Nerve nets are considered the evolutionarily oldest form of nervous system. How such networks develop and how complex nervous systems become fully functional is largely unknown. In a phylogenetically ancient animal, the freshwater polyp Hydra, we demonstrate how a nerve net consisting of distinct neuronal populations is precisely replicated over the course of asexual proliferation by budding. During this process, precursor cells first accumulate at the site of the emerging neural network, followed by a stepwise formation of functional neural circuits composed of distinct neuronal populations. These circuits become arranged according to an accurately controlled spatiotemporal pattern and take control of behaviors independently of the existing parental network. Since similar processes also govern the formation of more complex nervous systems in other invertebrates and vertebrates, we suggest that the basic requirements for a neuronal network to replicate were already in place at the beginning of the evolution of the nervous system.

title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity.
abstract: SIRPα is an inhibitory receptor with the canonical ligand CD47. Here, we show that human serine protease inhibitor A3 (SERPINA3) and its mouse ortholog SERPINA3k function as soluble binders and activators of SIRPα, suppressing SIRPα+ macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells and natural killer cells. SERPINA3(k) treatment alleviates lipopolysaccharide-induced pneumonia and ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis and rheumatoid arthritis. Although wild-type SERPINA3 provokes inflammation in cardiomyocytes and brain vascular endothelial cells, the SERPINA3D2 mutant, identified through functional domain mapping for SIRPα interaction, abolishes these adverse effects while retaining full inhibitory capacity. Notably, cancer cells secrete large amounts of SERPINA3(k), exceeding CD47 levels. Anti-SERPINA3(k) antibodies, used alone or in combination with blockade of programmed cell death 1 receptor/programmed cell death ligand 1, inhibit tumor growth in multiple preclinical models. This work identifies a potent soluble SIRPα ligand, offering effective therapeutic strategies for inflammatory/autoimmune diseases and a promising target for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
abstract: Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood. This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development. White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors. In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population. In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

title: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma and depression frequently co-occur, yet the mechanisms linking them remain unclear. Here, we show that chronic stress, systemic inflammation, or neuropathic pain are associated with hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice. Chronic stress hyperactivates a glutamatergic paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus → cholinergic dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus → liver circuit, increasing intratumoral acetylcholine. Single-cell transcriptomics identifies acetylcholine-responsive Chrna9+ epithelial cells that interact with macrophages through COL1A1/2-CD44-STAT3 signaling to promote CXCL1 production. Acetylcholine also promotes tumor cell proliferation through CHRNA9. Circulating CXCL1 crosses the blood-brain barrier and activates hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons, exacerbating depression-like behaviors and establishing a liver-brain feedback loop. Silencing the hypothalamic vagal circuit, tumor-specific Chrna9 knockdown, or systemic CXCL1 neutralization restrains tumor progression and alleviates depression-like behaviors. These findings identify a neural and immune mechanism linking chronic stress to hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.

title: Partial Loss of FITM2 Function Causes Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia.
abstract: FITM2 encodes fat storage-inducing transmembrane protein 2 (FIT2), a lipid diphosphatase in the ER that cleaves acyl-CoAs and is crucial for ER homeostasis. In humans, homozygous null mutations in FITM2 are associated with a syndrome characterized by deafness and dystonia. Here, we report two families presenting with late childhood-onset, slowly progressive limb spasticity, cerebellar features, and relatively preserved cognition, consistent with a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotype in whom exome sequencing revealed compound heterozygosity for FITM2 mutations. In each family, the affected probands carry one putative null allele and one G100R missense allele. Functional analyses demonstrated that the G100R allele is hypomorphic, with FIT2 protein levels reduced to 20% of wild type, leading to proportionately decreased enzyme activity. The occurrence of similar HSP disease phenotypes and the same hypomorphic mutation in these families suggests that the G100R mutation and its associated reduced enzyme activity represent a newly recognized clinical manifestation of FITM2 mutations, expanding the spectrum of conditions associated with this gene.

title: The "mobile bricks" of human evolution: how transposable elements shaped human phenotypes.
abstract: Far from being "junk" and devoid of function, transposable elements have been identified as players in genomes evolution and regulation, and are also used as valuable genetic markers to study population differentiation. Here we present a detailed review on how transposons participated in human evolution: from adaptation to extreme environments and response to both internal and external stressors, to phenotypes directly emerging from transposon mobilization activities. We dedicate a section to brain plasticity and neuronal differentiation, highlighting the possible role of transposable elements in neuro-psychiatric disorders in the context of emerging hypotheses such as the genomic trade-off and price-to-pay. Furthermore, we discuss methods and approaches to study the influence of transposable elements on human evolution, covering challenges to include ancient DNA in these studies. To conclude, we propose that transposons are not mere "background noise" in host genomes, but that they can be seen as genetic regulators of human phenotypes.

title: Leadership, burnout, and organizational mental health: a neuroscience-informed perspective.
abstract: This article argues that the persistent burden of burnout reflects a fundamental conceptual problem-burnout continues to be framed primarily as an individual condition rather than as an occupational phenomenon shaped by interacting structural, organizational, and leadership conditions. Burnout has emerged as a major occupational health challenge. In a 2024 survey across eight predominantly high and upper-middle-income countries, 48% of respondents reported currently grappling with burnout. Separately, depression and anxiety cost the global economy approximately one trillion dollars annually in lost productivity. Drawing on evidence from neuroimaging, stress biology, cognitive neuroscience, and organizational research, this article examines plausible pathways through which leadership behavior may influence conditions that contribute to or protect against burnout, including social threat-reward processing, cognitive flexibility, emotional intelligence, psychological safety, emotional contagion, and stress-related neurobiological responses. Among physicians, burnout has been associated with depression and anxiety, while evidence regarding substance abuse is less consistent. These proposed mechanisms are proximal and potentially modifiable, but operate within broader structural conditions that constrain or enable their effects. Human-centered work design and neuroleadership-informed leadership practices are proposed as complements to broader structural interventions, with implications for health systems, workforce sustainability, and policy design.

title: Identification of critical sites for glycine- and cesium-dependent activation of the RNA-edited glycine receptor α3L.
abstract: Glycine receptors (GlyRs) are chloride permeable ligand-gated ion channels that play an important role in synaptic transmission in the central nervous system. Besides glycine as neurotransmitter, cesium (Cs+) was shown to activate homomeric GlyRs with α2 and α3 subunits, and a recent study revealed the position D194 as essential for activation of RNA-edited GlyR α3185L at the cell surface. This position in the N-terminal extracellular ligand-binding domain belongs to a series of amino acid positions (D141, E192, D194 and D91, D97, E110, D114, Y161) predicted to be involved in Cs+ binding.
